newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LINDROS GOAL WITH 6.8 SECONDS LEFT LIFTS FLYERS PAST RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LINDROS GOAL WITH 6.8 SECONDS LEFT LIFTS FLYERS PAST RANGERS.

text.p: Eric Lindros's power-play goal with 6.8 seconds remaining gave the Philadephia Flyers a wild 3-2 victory over the New York Rangers Friday and a commanding 3-1 lead in the Eastern Conference finals.

Defenceman Jeff Beukeboom took a costly double-minor when his high-stick left Philadelphia's John LeClair bloodied with 1:35 to go. But the game appeared headed for overtime after New York goaltender Mike Richter came up with spectacular saves on Rod Brind'Amour and Lindros in the final 34 seconds.

The Rangers cleared the puck out of their zone with time running out, but the Flyers brought it right back. Brind'Amour left the puck for LeClair, who made a brilliant backhanded pass across the slot to Lindros at the left faceoff circle. He put a high backhander past a diving Richter for the game-winner.

It was the fourth goal in two games for Lindros, who is one win away from leading Philadelphia to its first Stanley Cup Finals since 1987. The Flyers can wrap up the series Sunday afternoon with a win at home in Game 5.
The third period featured a hectic ending for the second straight game as the teams combined for three goals in the final 3:13.

For a while, it appeared that it would be old nemesis John Druce, who would cripple the Rangers' playoff chances. Druce, who scored nine goals in five games against New York in the 1990 Patrick Division finals, got a shorthanded tally at 16:47 to break a 1-1 deadlock.
But the Rangers tied it just over a minute later. Wayne Gretzky passed from behind the net to Brian Leetch, who cut down the slot and banged home a shot from the top of the crease with 2:08 to play.
Mikael Renberg had scored on the power play at 7:08 of the first period to put Philadelphia up 1-0. Esa Tikkanen equalised at 1:41 of the third period on a shorthanded goal.
The Flyers had 40 shots on goal and the Rangers 34, with Ron Hextall in the Philadelphia goal.
